tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.

1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13	
14	Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
15	  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
16	  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
17	                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
18	  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
24	  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
25	  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())
26	
27	Traits:
28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.
33	
34	Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
35	  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
36	      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
37	
38	Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
39	  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
40	      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
41	  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
42	  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
43	  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
44	      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
45	      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
46	  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
47	      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
48	  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
49	      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).
50	Test fixtures: contracts/src/test_utils.rs exports ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE (const Address).

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

1	# Module migration brief (read fully before editing)
2	
3	Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust). We are migrating from Stylus SDK 0.9.0 +
4	motsu test framework to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 + the SDK's own testing framework (`stylus-test`,
5	exposed as `stylus_sdk::testing::*`, i.e. `TestVM`), on Rust 1.91.0 stable.
6	
7	Your worktree is the path given in your task. It is based on git commit 7e36233, which
8	already moved the manifests and the shared core (utils/address, utils/storage_slot,
9	proxy/erc1967/utils, utils/cryptography/eip712) to the new API. The crate does not
10	compile yet: other agents own the other modules and are fixing them in parallel.
11	
12	Read first:
13	- /tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md : the API decisions. Follow them exactly.
14	- The SDK source (read-only reference, do NOT build or run anything inside it):
15	  /tmp/bench/downloads/stylus-sdk-rs-0.10.10 . Useful paths: stylus-core/src/host.rs (VM
16	  accessor traits), stylus-core/src/calls/ (call contexts), stylus-sdk/src/call/ (call
17	  functions), stylus-test/README.md (TestVM usage), examples/ (SDK example contracts).
18	
19	## Ownership
20	Edit ONLY the files in your ownership list (given in your task). If you need a change in
21	a file you do not own, do not make it: list it under "requests" in your final report.
22	Never change a public item's name. Signature changes are allowed only as in api-map.md
23	or when needed to remove a global accessor (then document it in your report).
24	
25	## What "done" means for your files
26	1. Non-test code compiles on SDK 0.10.10 with NO global accessors: no `msg::`, `evm::`,
27	   `block::`, `contract::` free functions, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error, MethodError, Call,
28	   StaticCallContext}` (use `stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::{Error, MethodError}`;
29	   `Call`/`StaticCallContext` come from `stylus_sdk::prelude::*`). Host access is
30	   `self.vm()` (HostAccess) or the `context` parameter.
31	2. Every `pub trait I...` that is a public interface is tagged `#[public]`, and every
32	   `impl Trait for X` of such a trait is tagged `#[public]`. Traits with associated consts
33	   are NOT `#[public]`. Routed methods must be written in the `#[public] impl` block itself:
34	   default bodies in a `#[public]` trait are not routed.
35	3. Every motsu test is converted to a plain `#[test]` using `stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM`:
36	     let vm = TestVM::default();
37	     let mut c = Token::from(&vm);
38	     vm.set_sender(ALICE);            // msg::sender
39	     vm.set_value(U256::from(1));     // msg::value
40	     vm.set_block_timestamp(..); vm.set_chain_id(..); vm.set_balance(addr, v);
41	     vm.get_emitted_logs(); vm.mock_call(..); vm.mock_delegate_call(..); vm.mock_static_call(..)
42	   Use `crate::test_utils::{ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE}` instead of motsu's injected accounts.
43	   motsu's `Contract::<T>::new()` + `.sender(alice)` become `T::from(&vm)` + `vm.set_sender`.
44	   Property tests (proptest inside a test) must build a fresh TestVM per case.
45	4. Preserve every test scenario and every assertion. Do NOT delete, weaken, or merge away a
46	   test unless it is an exact duplicate of another test in the same file (then say so).
47	   Keep `#[should_panic]`/revert checks as revert checks (`is_err()` / matching the error).
48	5. Do NOT change storage layout: field order and field types of every `#[storage]`
49	   struct stay byte-for-byte the same. (Proxies depend on it.)
50	6. Preserve the public ABI: function names, selectors, parameter and return types, error
51	   types and their encodings. Preserve behavior. Only the Rust-level API for host access
52	   may change (documented in the report).
53	7. Rustdoc stays accurate: where the call pattern changed (context/self.vm()), update the
54	   doc text. No commented-out code, no TODO left for things you were asked to do.
55	8. `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `use super::*;` and explicit imports as the rest of the repo.
56	
57	## Verification (use the 1.91.0 toolchain; never use nightly for building)
58	- Check your files only:
59	    cd <worktree> && cargo +1.91.0 check -p openzeppelin-stylus > /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log 2>&1
60	    grep -A1 '^error' /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log | grep -- '--> ' | sed 's/.*--> //' | sort | uniq -c
61	  Only errors in YOUR files matter until the whole crate compiles.
62	- Tests: `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib <filter>` runs only once the whole
63	  test target compiles. Until then, check your test code with
64	  `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib --no-run` and filter errors to your files.
65	- Formatting: `rustfmt +nightly-2025-08-01 --edition 2021 <your files>` (the repo's
66	  rustfmt.toml uses options only nightly rustfmt supports). Run it on your files at the end.
67	- Clippy (once the crate compiles): `cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p openzeppelin-stylus --all-targets -- -D warnings`
68	  Lints are pedantic (see workspace Cargo.toml). Fix warnings in your files.
69	
70	## Git
71	- Work and commit on your branch (already created for your worktree). Small logical commits,
72	  message style: `refactor(<area>): <what>` or `test(<area>): <what>`. Each message ends with:
73	    Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
74	- Commit only your files. Do not push. Do not switch branches. Do not run `git reset --hard`
75	  or any command that touches other worktrees.
76	
77	## Final report (your last message, at most 40 lines)
78	- Files changed; commit list (`git log --oneline 7e36233..HEAD`).
79	- Signature changes (name: old -> new).
80	- Test inventory: number of test functions before (`git show 7e36233:<file> | grep -cE '#\[(motsu::)?test\]'`)
81	  and after, per file; any test you merged or removed (with reason).
82	- Compile status of your files (lib / tests); whether the crate compiled as a whole at the time.
83	- Requests to other owners; blockers; anything you were unsure about.
84

1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13	
14	Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
15	  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
16	  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
17	                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
18	  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
24	  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
25	  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())
26	
27	Traits:
28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.
33	
34	Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
35	  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
36	      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
37	
38	Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
39	  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
40	      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
41	  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
42	  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
43	  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
44	      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
45	      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
46	  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
47	      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
48	  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
49	      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).
50	Test fixtures: contracts/src/test_utils.rs exports ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE (const Address).

/*!
# OpenZeppelin Contracts for Stylus

A library for secure smart contract development written in Rust for
[Arbitrum Stylus](https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/gentle-introduction).
This library offers common smart contract primitives and affordances that take
advantage of the nature of Stylus.

## Usage

To start using it, add `openzeppelin-stylus` to your `Cargo.toml`, or simply run
`cargo add openzeppelin-stylus`.

```toml
[dependencies]
openzeppelin-stylus = "x.x.x"
```

We recommend pinning to a specific version -- expect rapid iteration.

Once defined as a dependency, use one of our pre-defined implementations by
importing them:

```ignore
use openzeppelin_stylus::token::erc20::{self, Erc20, IErc20};
use stylus_sdk::{alloy_primitives::{Address, U256}, prelude::*};

#[entrypoint]
#[storage]
struct MyContract {
    pub erc20: Erc20}

#[public]
#[implements(IErc20<Error = erc20::Error>)]
impl MyContract {}

#[public]
impl IErc20 for MyContract {
    type Error = erc20::Error;

    fn total_supply(&self) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.total_supply()
    }

    fn balance_of(&self, account: Address) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.balance_of(account)
    }

    fn transfer(
        &mut self,
        to: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.transfer(to, value)
    }

    fn allowance(&self, owner: Address, spender: Address) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.allowance(owner, spender)
    }

    fn approve(
        &mut self,
        spender: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.approve(spender, value)
    }

    fn transfer_from(
        &mut self,
        from: Address,
        to: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.transfer_from(from, to, value)
    }
}
```
*/

23	    /// to the ecrecover operation.
24	    pub mod ecrecover {
25	        pub use crate::utils::cryptography::ecdsa::{

31	/// Trait providing access to Arbitrum precompiles for Stylus contracts.
32	///
33	/// This trait wraps complex precompile invocations to provide a clean,
34	/// ergonomic interface for calling Arbitrum's built-in cryptographic functions
35	/// and utilities from within Stylus smart contracts.
36	///
37	/// Precompiles are pre-deployed contracts at fixed addresses that implement
38	/// commonly used cryptographic operations and other utilities. They execute
39	/// natively in the Arbitrum runtime for better performance compared to
40	/// implementing these operations in contract code.
41	///
42	/// See: <https://docs.arbitrum.io/build-decentralized-apps/precompiles/overview>
43	///
44	/// # Usage
45	///
46	/// Implement this trait for your contract storage type to gain access to
47	/// precompile functionality:
48	///
49	/// ```rust,ignore
50	/// use openzeppelin_stylus::utils::cryptography::Precompiles;
51	///
52	/// #[storage]
53	/// #[entrypoint]
54	/// struct MyContract {
55	///     // your fields...
56	/// }
57	///
58	/// // The `Precompiles` trait is automatically implemented for all
59	/// // contracts annotated with `#[entrypoint]` or that implement
60	/// // `stylus_sdk::prelude::TopLevelStorage`.
61	///
62	/// #[public]
63	/// impl MyContract {
64	///     fn verify_signature(&mut self, msg_hash: B256, sig: (u8, B256, B256)) -> Result<Address, Error> {
65	///         let (v, r, s) = sig;
66	///         self.ec_recover(msg_hash, v, r, s)
67	///     }
68	/// }
69	/// ```
70	///
71	/// # Error Handling
72	///
73	/// Precompile methods return `Result` types to handle both invalid inputs and
74	/// precompile execution failures. Always handle these errors appropriately
75	/// in your contract logic.
76	pub trait Precompiles: TopLevelStorage {
77	    /// Recovers the address that signed a hashed message (`hash`) using an
78	    /// ECDSA signature (v, r, s).
79	    ///
80	    /// Wrapper around the `ecRecover` precompile.
81	    ///
82	    /// # Arguments
83	    ///
84	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
85	    /// * `hash` - Hash of the message.
86	    /// * `v` - `v` value from the signature.
87	    /// * `r` - `r` value from the signature.
88	    /// * `s` - `s` value from the signature.
89	    ///
90	    /// # Errors
91	    ///
92	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSignatureS`] - If the `s` value is grater than
93	    ///   [`primitives::ecrecover::SIGNATURE_S_UPPER_BOUND`].
94	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSignature`] - If the recovered address is
95	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
96	    ///
97	    /// # Panics
98	    ///
99	    /// * If the `ecRecover` precompile fails to execute.
100	    fn ec_recover(
101	        &self,
102	        hash: B256,
103	        v: u8,
104	        r: B256,
105	        s: B256,
106	    ) -> Result<Address, Error>;
107	
108	    /// Performs signature verifications in the `secp256r1` elliptic curve.
109	    ///
110	    /// Wrapper around the `P256VERIFY` precompile introduced in [RIP-7212].
111	    ///
112	    /// [RIP-7212]: https://github.com/ethereum/RIPs/blob/723155c3d86427412b5bc0f98ad1e4791ea7347f/RIPS/rip-7212.md
113	    ///
114	    /// # Arguments
115	    ///
116	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
117	    /// * `hash` - Signed data hash.
118	    /// * `r` - `r` component of the signature.
119	    /// * `s` - `s` component of the signature.
120	    /// * `x` - `x` coordinate of the public key.
121	    /// * `y` - `y` coordinate of the public key.
122	    fn p256_verify(
123	        &self,
124	        hash: B256,
125	        r: B256,
126	        s: B256,
127	        x: B256,
128	        y: B256,
129	    ) -> bool;
130	}
131	
132	impl<T: TopLevelStorage> Precompiles for T {
133	    fn ec_recover(
134	        &self,
135	        hash: B256,
136	        v: u8,
137	        r: B256,
138	        s: B256,
139	    ) -> Result<Address, Error> {
140	        recover(self, hash, v, r, s)
141	    }
142	
143	    fn p256_verify(
144	        &self,
145	        hash: B256,
146	        r: B256,
147	        s: B256,
148	        x: B256,
149	        y: B256,
150	    ) -> bool {
151	        p256_verify(self, hash, r, s, x, y)
152	    }
153	}

13	/// The host trait defines methods a Stylus contract can use to interact
14	/// with a host environment, such as the EVM. It is a composition
15	/// of traits with different access to host values and modifications.
16	/// Stylus contracts in the SDK have access to a host via the [`HostAccess`] trait for safe access
17	/// to hostios without the need for global invocations. The host trait may be implemented
18	/// by test frameworks as an easier way of mocking hostio invocations for testing
19	/// Stylus contracts.
20	pub trait Host:
21	    CryptographyAccess
22	    + CalldataAccess
23	    + UnsafeDeploymentAccess
24	    + StorageAccess
25	    + UnsafeCallAccess
26	    + BlockAccess
27	    + ChainAccess
28	    + AccountAccess
29	    + MemoryAccess
30	    + MessageAccess
31	    + MeteringAccess
32	    + RawLogAccess
33	    + DynClone
34	{
35	}
36	
37	// Enables cloning of a boxed, host trait object.
38	dyn_clone::clone_trait_object!(Host);
39	
40	/// Defines a trait that allows a Stylus contract to access its host safely.
41	pub trait HostAccess {
42	    /// Host type returned by [`Self::vm()`].
43	    type Host: Host;
44	
45	    /// Provides access to the parametrized host of a contract, giving access
46	    /// to all the desired hostios from the user.
47	    fn vm(&self) -> &Self::Host;
48	}
49	
50	/// Defines a trait that can deny access to a contract router method if a message value is
51	/// passed in while the method is non-payable.
52	pub trait ValueDenier {
53	    fn deny_value(&self, method_name: &str) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>>;
54	}
55	
56	/// Defines a trait that guards whether the constructor was already called.
57	pub trait ConstructorGuard {
58	    fn check_constructor_slot(&self) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>>;
59	}
60	
61	/// Provides access to native cryptography extensions provided by
62	/// a Stylus contract host, such as keccak256.
63	pub trait CryptographyAccess {
64	    /// Efficiently computes the [`keccak256`] hash of the given preimage.
65	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`SHA3`] opcode.
66	    ///

100	/// Provides access to programmatic creation of contracts via the host environment's CREATE
101	/// and CREATE2 opcodes in the EVM.
102	///
103	/// # Safety
104	/// These methods should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access
105	/// to create1 and create2 opcodes is needed. Using the methods by themselves will not protect
106	/// against reentrancy safety, storage aliasing, or cache flushing. For safe contract deployment,
107	/// utilize a [`RawDeploy`] struct instead.
108	pub unsafe trait UnsafeDeploymentAccess {
109	    /// Deploys a new contract using the init code provided, which the EVM executes to construct
110	    /// the code of the newly deployed contract. The init code must be written in EVM bytecode, but
111	    /// the code it deploys can be that of a Stylus program. The code returned will be treated as
112	    /// WASM if it begins with the EOF-inspired header `0xEFF0`. Otherwise the code will be
113	    /// interpreted as that of a traditional EVM-style contract. See [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]
114	    /// for more information on writing init code.
115	    ///
116	    /// On success, this hostio returns the address of the newly created account whose address is
117	    /// a function of the sender and nonce. On failure the address will be `0`, `return_data_len`
118	    /// will store the length of the revert data, the bytes of which can be read via the
119	    /// `read_return_data` hostio. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`CREATE`]
120	    /// opcode, which notably includes the exact address returned.
121	    ///
122	    /// [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/quickstart
123	    /// [`CREATE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f0
124	    ///
125	    /// # Safety
126	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to create1 is
127	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
128	    /// Utilize a [`RawDeploy`] struct instead for safety.
129	    unsafe fn create1(
130	        &self,
131	        code: *const u8,
132	        code_len: usize,
133	        endowment: *const u8,
134	        contract: *mut u8,
135	        revert_data_len: *mut usize,
136	    );
137	    /// Deploys a new contract using the init code provided, which the EVM executes to construct
138	    /// the code of the newly deployed contract. The init code must be written in EVM bytecode, but
139	    /// the code it deploys can be that of a Stylus program. The code returned will be treated as
140	    /// WASM if it begins with the EOF-inspired header `0xEFF0`. Otherwise the code will be
141	    /// interpreted as that of a traditional EVM-style contract. See [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]
142	    /// for more information on writing init code.
143	    ///
144	    /// On success, this hostio returns the address of the newly created account whose address is a
145	    /// function of the sender, salt, and init code. On failure the address will be `0`,
146	    /// `return_data_len` will store the length of the revert data, the bytes of which can be read
147	    /// via the `read_return_data` hostio. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
148	    /// `[CREATE2`] opcode, which notably includes the exact address returned.
149	    ///
150	    /// [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/quickstart
151	    /// [`CREATE2`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f5
152	    ///
153	    /// # Safety
154	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to create2 is
155	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
156	    /// Utilize a [`RawDeploy`] struct instead for safety.
157	    unsafe fn create2(
158	        &self,
159	        code: *const u8,
160	        code_len: usize,
161	        endowment: *const u8,
162	        salt: *const u8,
163	        contract: *mut u8,
164	        revert_data_len: *mut usize,
165	    );
166	}

168	/// Provides access to storage access and mutation via host methods.
169	pub trait StorageAccess {
170	    /// Reads a 32-byte value from permanent storage. Stylus's storage format is identical to
171	    /// that of the EVM. This means that, under the hood, this hostio is accessing the 32-byte
172	    /// value stored in the EVM state trie at offset `key`, which will be `0` when not previously
173	    /// set. The semantics, then, are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`SLOAD`] opcode.
174	    ///
175	    /// Note: the Stylus VM implements storage caching. This means that repeated calls to the same
176	    /// key will cost less than in the EVM.
177	    ///
178	    /// [`SLOAD`]: https://www.evm.codes/#54
179	    fn storage_load_bytes32(&self, key: U256) -> B256;
180	    /// Writes a 32-byte value to the permanent storage cache. Stylus's storage format is identical
181	    /// to that of the EVM. This means that, under the hood, this hostio represents storing a
182	    /// 32-byte value into the EVM state trie at offset `key`. Refunds are tabulated exactly as
183	    /// in the EVM. The semantics, then, are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`SSTORE`] opcode.
184	    ///
185	    /// Note: because the value is cached, one must call `flush_cache` to persist it.
186	    ///
187	    /// [`SSTORE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#55
188	    ///
189	    /// # Safety
190	    /// May alias storage.
191	    unsafe fn storage_cache_bytes32(&self, key: U256, value: B256);
192	    /// Persists any dirty values in the storage cache to the EVM state trie, dropping the cache
193	    /// entirely if requested. Analogous to repeated invocations of [`SSTORE`].
194	    ///
195	    /// [`SSTORE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#55
196	    fn flush_cache(&self, clear: bool);
197	}

199	/// Provides access to calling other contracts using host semantics.
200	///
201	/// # Safety
202	/// These methods should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access
203	/// to call, static_call, and delegate_call methods is required. Using the methods by themselves
204	/// will not protect against reentrancy safety, storage aliasing, or cache flushing. For safe
205	/// contract calls, utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead.
206	pub unsafe trait UnsafeCallAccess {
207	    /// Calls the contract at the given address with options for passing value and to limit the
208	    /// amount of gas supplied. The return status indicates whether the call succeeded, and is
209	    /// nonzero on failure.
210	    ///
211	    /// In both cases `return_data_len` will store the length of the result, the bytes of which can
212	    /// be read via the `read_return_data` hostio. The bytes are not returned directly so that the
213	    /// programmer can potentially save gas by choosing which subset of the return result they'd
214	    /// like to copy.
215	    ///
216	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`CALL`] opcode, including callvalue
217	    /// stipends and the 63/64 gas rule. This means that supplying the `u64::MAX` gas can be used
218	    /// to send as much as possible.
219	    ///
220	    /// [`CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f1
221	    ///
222	    /// # Safety
223	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to calls is
224	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
225	    /// Utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead for safety.
226	    unsafe fn call_contract(
227	        &self,
228	        to: *const u8,
229	        data: *const u8,
230	        data_len: usize,
231	        value: *const u8,
232	        gas: u64,
233	        outs_len: &mut usize,
234	    ) -> u8;
235	    /// Static calls the contract at the given address, with the option to limit the amount of gas
236	    /// supplied. The return status indicates whether the call succeeded, and is nonzero on
237	    /// failure.
238	    ///
239	    /// In both cases `return_data_len` will store the length of the result, the bytes of which can
240	    /// be read via the `read_return_data` hostio. The bytes are not returned directly so that the
241	    /// programmer can potentially save gas by choosing which subset of the return result they'd
242	    /// like to copy.
243	    ///
244	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`STATIC_CALL`] opcode, including the
245	    /// 63/64 gas rule. This means that supplying `u64::MAX` gas can be used to send as much as
246	    /// possible.
247	    ///
248	    /// [`STATIC_CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#FA
249	    ///
250	    /// # Safety
251	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to calls is
252	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
253	    /// Utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead for safety.
254	    unsafe fn static_call_contract(
255	        &self,
256	        to: *const u8,
257	        data: *const u8,
258	        data_len: usize,
259	        gas: u64,
260	        outs_len: &mut usize,
261	    ) -> u8;
262	    /// Delegate calls the contract at the given address, with the option to limit the amount of
263	    /// gas supplied. The return status indicates whether the call succeeded, and is nonzero on
264	    /// failure.
265	    ///
266	    /// In both cases `return_data_len` will store the length of the result, the bytes of which
267	    /// can be read via the `read_return_data` hostio. The bytes are not returned directly so that
268	    /// the programmer can potentially save gas by choosing which subset of the return result
269	    /// they'd like to copy.
270	    ///
271	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`DELEGATE_CALL`] opcode, including the
272	    /// 63/64 gas rule. This means that supplying `u64::MAX` gas can be used to send as much as
273	    /// possible.
274	    ///
275	    /// [`DELEGATE_CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#F4
276	    ///
277	    /// # Safety
278	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to calls is
279	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
280	    /// Utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead for safety.
281	    unsafe fn delegate_call_contract(
282	        &self,
283	        to: *const u8,
284	        data: *const u8,
285	        data_len: usize,
286	        gas: u64,
287	        outs_len: &mut usize,
288	    ) -> u8;
289	}

404	/// Provides access to metering values such as EVM gas and Stylus ink used and remaining,
405	/// as well as details of their prices based on the host environment.
406	pub trait MeteringAccess {
407	    /// Gets the amount of gas left after paying for the cost of this hostio. The semantics are
408	    /// equivalent to that of the EVM's [`GAS`] opcode.
409	    ///
410	    /// [`GAS`]: https://www.evm.codes/#5a
411	    fn evm_gas_left(&self) -> u64;
412	    /// Gets the amount of ink remaining after paying for the cost of this hostio. The semantics
413	    /// are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`GAS`] opcode, except the units are in ink. See
414	    /// [`Ink and Gas`] for more information on Stylus's compute pricing.
415	    ///
416	    /// [`GAS`]: https://www.evm.codes/#5a
417	    /// [`Ink and Gas`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/concepts/gas-metering
418	    fn evm_ink_left(&self) -> u64;
419	    /// Gets the gas price in wei per gas, which on Arbitrum chains equals the basefee. The
420	    /// semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`GAS_PRICE`] opcode.
421	    ///
422	    /// [`GAS_PRICE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3A
423	    fn tx_gas_price(&self) -> U256;
424	    /// Gets the price of ink in evm gas basis points. See [`Ink and Gas`] for more information on
425	    /// Stylus's compute-pricing model. Arbitrum enforces a minimum gas price floor, so tx ink
426	    /// price should always return a value greater than zero.
427	    ///
428	    /// [`Ink and Gas`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/concepts/gas-metering
429	    fn tx_ink_price(&self) -> u32;
430	
431	    /// Computes the units of gas per a specified amount of ink.
432	    fn ink_to_gas(&self, ink: u64) -> u64 {
433	        let price = self.tx_ink_price();
434	        if price == 0 {
435	            return 0;
436	        }
437	        ink / price as u64
438	    }
439	
440	    /// Computes the units of ink per a specified amount of gas.
441	    fn gas_to_ink(&self, gas: u64) -> u64 {
442	        gas.saturating_mul(self.tx_ink_price().into())
443	    }
444	}

463	/// Provides access to the ability to emit typed logs from a Stylus contract.
464	pub trait LogAccess: RawLogAccess {
465	    /// Emits a typed alloy log.
466	    ///
467	    /// ```rust,ignore
468	    /// sol! {
469	    ///    event Transfer(
470	    ///        address indexed from,
471	    ///        address indexed to,
472	    ///        uint256 indexed token_id
473	    ///    );
474	    /// }
475	    ///
476	    /// self.vm().log(Transfer { from, to, token_id });
477	    /// ```
478	    fn log<T: SolEvent>(&self, event: T) {
479	        // According to the alloy docs, encode_topics_raw fails only if the array is too small
480	
481	        let mut topics = [WordToken::default(); 4];
482	        event.encode_topics_raw(&mut topics).unwrap();
483	
484	        let count = T::TopicList::COUNT;
485	        let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(32 * count);
486	        for topic in &topics[..count] {
487	            bytes.extend_from_slice(topic.as_slice());
488	        }
489	        event.encode_data_to(&mut bytes);
490	        self.emit_log(&bytes, count)
491	    }
492	}

100	/// Provides access to programmatic creation of contracts via the host environment's CREATE
101	/// and CREATE2 opcodes in the EVM.

103	/// # Safety
104	/// These methods should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access
105	/// to create1 and create2 opcodes is needed. Using the methods by themselves will not protect
106	/// against reentrancy safety, storage aliasing, or cache flushing. For safe contract deployment,
107	/// utilize a [`RawDeploy`] struct instead.
108	pub unsafe trait UnsafeDeploymentAccess {
109	    /// Deploys a new contract using the init code provided, which the EVM executes to construct
110	    /// the code of the newly deployed contract. The init code must be written in EVM bytecode, but
111	    /// the code it deploys can be that of a Stylus program. The code returned will be treated as
112	    /// WASM if it begins with the EOF-inspired header `0xEFF0`. Otherwise the code will be
113	    /// interpreted as that of a traditional EVM-style contract. See [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]
114	    /// for more information on writing init code.
115	    ///
116	    /// On success, this hostio returns the address of the newly created account whose address is
117	    /// a function of the sender and nonce. On failure the address will be `0`, `return_data_len`
118	    /// will store the length of the revert data, the bytes of which can be read via the
119	    /// `read_return_data` hostio. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`CREATE`]
120	    /// opcode, which notably includes the exact address returned.
121	    ///
122	    /// [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/quickstart
123	    /// [`CREATE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f0
124	    ///
125	    /// # Safety
126	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to create1 is
127	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
128	    /// Utilize a [`RawDeploy`] struct instead for safety.
129	    unsafe fn create1(
130	        &self,
131	        code: *const u8,
132	        code_len: usize,
133	        endowment: *const u8,
134	        contract: *mut u8,
135	        revert_data_len: *mut usize,
136	    );
137	    /// Deploys a new contract using the init code provided, which the EVM executes to construct
138	    /// the code of the newly deployed contract. The init code must be written in EVM bytecode, but
139	    /// the code it deploys can be that of a Stylus program. The code returned will be treated as
140	    /// WASM if it begins with the EOF-inspired header `0xEFF0`. Otherwise the code will be
141	    /// interpreted as that of a traditional EVM-style contract. See [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]
142	    /// for more information on writing init code.
143	    ///
144	    /// On success, this hostio returns the address of the newly created account whose address is a
145	    /// function of the sender, salt, and init code. On failure the address will be `0`,
146	    /// `return_data_len` will store the length of the revert data, the bytes of which can be read
147	    /// via the `read_return_data` hostio. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
148	    /// `[CREATE2`] opcode, which notably includes the exact address returned.
149	    ///
150	    /// [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/quickstart
151	    /// [`CREATE2`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f5
152	    ///
153	    /// # Safety
154	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to create2 is
155	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
156	    /// Utilize a [`RawDeploy`] struct instead for safety.
157	    unsafe fn create2(
158	        &self,
159	        code: *const u8,
160	        code_len: usize,
161	        endowment: *const u8,
162	        salt: *const u8,
163	        contract: *mut u8,
164	        revert_data_len: *mut usize,
165	    );
166	}

168	/// Provides access to storage access and mutation via host methods.
169	pub trait StorageAccess {
170	    /// Reads a 32-byte value from permanent storage. Stylus's storage format is identical to
171	    /// that of the EVM. This means that, under the hood, this hostio is accessing the 32-byte
172	    /// value stored in the EVM state trie at offset `key`, which will be `0` when not previously
173	    /// set. The semantics, then, are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`SLOAD`] opcode.
174	    ///
175	    /// Note: the Stylus VM implements storage caching. This means that repeated calls to the same
176	    /// key will cost less than in the EVM.
177	    ///
178	    /// [`SLOAD`]: https://www.evm.codes/#54
179	    fn storage_load_bytes32(&self, key: U256) -> B256;
180	    /// Writes a 32-byte value to the permanent storage cache. Stylus's storage format is identical
181	    /// to that of the EVM. This means that, under the hood, this hostio represents storing a
182	    /// 32-byte value into the EVM state trie at offset `key`. Refunds are tabulated exactly as
183	    /// in the EVM. The semantics, then, are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`SSTORE`] opcode.
184	    ///
185	    /// Note: because the value is cached, one must call `flush_cache` to persist it.
186	    ///
187	    /// [`SSTORE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#55
188	    ///
189	    /// # Safety
190	    /// May alias storage.
191	    unsafe fn storage_cache_bytes32(&self, key: U256, value: B256);
192	    /// Persists any dirty values in the storage cache to the EVM state trie, dropping the cache
193	    /// entirely if requested. Analogous to repeated invocations of [`SSTORE`].
194	    ///
195	    /// [`SSTORE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#55
196	    fn flush_cache(&self, clear: bool);
197	}

199	/// Provides access to calling other contracts using host semantics.
200	///
201	/// # Safety
202	/// These methods should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access
203	/// to call, static_call, and delegate_call methods is required. Using the methods by themselves
204	/// will not protect against reentrancy safety, storage aliasing, or cache flushing. For safe
205	/// contract calls, utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead.
206	pub unsafe trait UnsafeCallAccess {
207	    /// Calls the contract at the given address with options for passing value and to limit the
208	    /// amount of gas supplied. The return status indicates whether the call succeeded, and is
209	    /// nonzero on failure.
210	    ///
211	    /// In both cases `return_data_len` will store the length of the result, the bytes of which can
212	    /// be read via the `read_return_data` hostio. The bytes are not returned directly so that the
213	    /// programmer can potentially save gas by choosing which subset of the return result they'd
214	    /// like to copy.
215	    ///
216	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`CALL`] opcode, including callvalue
217	    /// stipends and the 63/64 gas rule. This means that supplying the `u64::MAX` gas can be used
218	    /// to send as much as possible.
219	    ///
220	    /// [`CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f1
221	    ///
222	    /// # Safety
223	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to calls is
224	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
225	    /// Utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead for safety.
226	    unsafe fn call_contract(
227	        &self,
228	        to: *const u8,
229	        data: *const u8,
230	        data_len: usize,
231	        value: *const u8,
232	        gas: u64,
233	        outs_len: &mut usize,
234	    ) -> u8;
235	    /// Static calls the contract at the given address, with the option to limit the amount of gas
236	    /// supplied. The return status indicates whether the call succeeded, and is nonzero on
237	    /// failure.
238	    ///
239	    /// In both cases `return_data_len` will store the length of the result, the bytes of which can
240	    /// be read via the `read_return_data` hostio. The bytes are not returned directly so that the
241	    /// programmer can potentially save gas by choosing which subset of the return result they'd
242	    /// like to copy.
243	    ///
244	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`STATIC_CALL`] opcode, including the
245	    /// 63/64 gas rule. This means that supplying `u64::MAX` gas can be used to send as much as
246	    /// possible.
247	    ///
248	    /// [`STATIC_CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#FA
249	    ///
250	    /// # Safety
251	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to calls is
252	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
253	    /// Utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead for safety.
254	    unsafe fn static_call_contract(
255	        &self,
256	        to: *const u8,
257	        data: *const u8,
258	        data_len: usize,
259	        gas: u64,
260	        outs_len: &mut usize,
261	    ) -> u8;
262	    /// Delegate calls the contract at the given address, with the option to limit the amount of
263	    /// gas supplied. The return status indicates whether the call succeeded, and is nonzero on
264	    /// failure.
265	    ///
266	    /// In both cases `return_data_len` will store the length of the result, the bytes of which
267	    /// can be read via the `read_return_data` hostio. The bytes are not returned directly so that
268	    /// the programmer can potentially save gas by choosing which subset of the return result
269	    /// they'd like to copy.
270	    ///
271	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`DELEGATE_CALL`] opcode, including the
272	    /// 63/64 gas rule. This means that supplying `u64::MAX` gas can be used to send as much as
273	    /// possible.
274	    ///
275	    /// [`DELEGATE_CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#F4
276	    ///
277	    /// # Safety
278	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to calls is
279	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
280	    /// Utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead for safety.
281	    unsafe fn delegate_call_contract(
282	        &self,
283	        to: *const u8,
284	        data: *const u8,
285	        data_len: usize,
286	        gas: u64,
287	        outs_len: &mut usize,
288	    ) -> u8;
289	}

291	/// Provides access to host methods relating to the block a transaction
292	/// to a Stylus contract is included in.
293	pub trait BlockAccess {
294	    /// Gets the basefee of the current block. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
295	    /// [`BASEFEE`] opcode.
296	    ///
297	    /// [`BASEFEE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#48
298	    fn block_basefee(&self) -> U256;
299	    /// Gets the coinbase of the current block, which on Arbitrum chains is the L1 batch poster's
300	    /// address. This differs from Ethereum where the validator including the transaction
301	    /// determines the coinbase.
302	    fn block_coinbase(&self) -> Address;
303	    /// Gets a bounded estimate of the L1 block number at which the Sequencer sequenced the
304	    /// transaction. See [`Block Numbers and Time`] for more information on how this value is

317	    /// implies that the opcode returns the gas limit of the current transaction.  When in doubt,
318	    /// consult [`The Ethereum Yellow Paper`].
319	    ///
320	    /// [`GAS_LIMIT`]: https://www.evm.codes/#45
321	    /// [`The Ethereum Yellow Paper`]: https://ethereum.github.io/yellowpaper/paper.pdf
322	    fn block_gas_limit(&self) -> u64;
323	}

325	/// Provides access to the chain details of the host environment.
326	pub trait ChainAccess {
327	    /// Gets the unique chain identifier of the Arbitrum chain. The semantics are equivalent to
328	    /// that of the EVM's [`CHAIN_ID`] opcode.
329	    ///
330	    /// [`CHAIN_ID`]: https://www.evm.codes/#46
331	    fn chain_id(&self) -> u64;
332	}

334	/// Provides access to account details of addresses of the host environment.
335	pub trait AccountAccess {
336	    /// Gets the ETH balance in wei of the account at the given address.
337	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`BALANCE`] opcode.
338	    ///
339	    /// [`BALANCE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#31
340	    fn balance(&self, account: Address) -> U256;
341	    /// Gets the address of the current program. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
342	    /// [`ADDRESS`] opcode.
343	    ///
344	    /// [`ADDRESS`]: https://www.evm.codes/#30
345	    fn contract_address(&self) -> Address;
346	    /// Gets a subset of the code from the account at the given address. The semantics are identical
347	    /// to that of the EVM's [`EXT_CODE_COPY`] opcode, aside from one small detail: the write to
348	    /// the buffer `dest` will stop after the last byte is written. This is unlike the EVM,
349	    /// which right pads with zeros in this scenario. The return value is the number of bytes
350	    /// written, which allows the caller to detect if this has occurred.
351	    ///
352	    /// [`EXT_CODE_COPY`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3C
353	    fn code(&self, account: Address) -> Vec<u8>;
354	    /// Gets the size of the code in bytes at the given address. The semantics are equivalent
355	    /// to that of the EVM's [`EXT_CODESIZE`].
356	    ///
357	    /// [`EXT_CODESIZE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3B
358	    fn code_size(&self, account: Address) -> usize;
359	    /// Gets the code hash of the account at the given address. The semantics are equivalent
360	    /// to that of the EVM's [`EXT_CODEHASH`] opcode. Note that the code hash of an account without
361	    /// code will be the empty hash
362	    /// `keccak("") = c5d2460186f7233c927e7db2dcc703c0e500b653ca82273b7bfad8045d85a470`.
363	    ///
364	    /// [`EXT_CODEHASH`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3F
365	    fn code_hash(&self, account: Address) -> B256;
366	}

368	/// Provides the ability to pay for memory growth of a Stylus contract.
369	pub trait MemoryAccess {
370	    /// The `entrypoint!` macro handles importing this hostio, which is required if the
371	    /// program's memory grows. Otherwise compilation through the `ArbWasm` precompile will revert.
372	    /// Internally the Stylus VM forces calls to this hostio whenever new WASM pages are allocated.
373	    /// Calls made voluntarily will unproductively consume gas.
374	    fn pay_for_memory_grow(&self, pages: u16);
375	}
376	
377	/// Provides access to transaction details of a Stylus contract.
378	pub trait MessageAccess {
379	    /// Gets the address of the account that called the program. For normal L2-to-L2 transactions
380	    /// the semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`CALLER`] opcode, including in cases
381	    /// arising from [`DELEGATE_CALL`].
382	    ///
383	    /// For L1-to-L2 retryable ticket transactions, the top-level sender's address will be aliased.
384	    /// See [`Retryable Ticket Address Aliasing`] for more information on how this works.
385	    ///
386	    /// [`CALLER`]: https://www.evm.codes/#33
387	    /// [`DELEGATE_CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f4
388	    /// [`Retryable Ticket Address Aliasing`]: https://developer.arbitrum.io/arbos/l1-to-l2-messaging#address-aliasing
389	    fn msg_sender(&self) -> Address;
390	    /// Whether the current call is reentrant.
391	    fn msg_reentrant(&self) -> bool;
392	    /// Get the ETH value in wei sent to the program. The semantics are equivalent to that of the
393	    /// EVM's [`CALLVALUE`] opcode.
394	    ///
395	    /// [`CALLVALUE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#34
396	    fn msg_value(&self) -> U256;
397	    /// Gets the top-level sender of the transaction. The semantics are equivalent to that of the
398	    /// EVM's [`ORIGIN`] opcode.
399	    ///
400	    /// [`ORIGIN`]: https://www.evm.codes/#32
401	    fn tx_origin(&self) -> Address;
402	}
403	
404	/// Provides access to metering values such as EVM gas and Stylus ink used and remaining,
405	/// as well as details of their prices based on the host environment.
406	pub trait MeteringAccess {
407	    /// Gets the amount of gas left after paying for the cost of this hostio. The semantics are
408	    /// equivalent to that of the EVM's [`GAS`] opcode.
409	    ///
410	    /// [`GAS`]: https://www.evm.codes/#5a
411	    fn evm_gas_left(&self) -> u64;
412	    /// Gets the amount of ink remaining after paying for the cost of this hostio. The semantics
413	    /// are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`GAS`] opcode, except the units are in ink. See
414	    /// [`Ink and Gas`] for more information on Stylus's compute pricing.
415	    ///
416	    /// [`GAS`]: https://www.evm.codes/#5a
417	    /// [`Ink and Gas`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/concepts/gas-metering
418	    fn evm_ink_left(&self) -> u64;
419	    /// Gets the gas price in wei per gas, which on Arbitrum chains equals the basefee. The
420	    /// semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`GAS_PRICE`] opcode.
421	    ///
422	    /// [`GAS_PRICE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3A
423	    fn tx_gas_price(&self) -> U256;
424	    /// Gets the price of ink in evm gas basis points. See [`Ink and Gas`] for more information on
425	    /// Stylus's compute-pricing model. Arbitrum enforces a minimum gas price floor, so tx ink
426	    /// price should always return a value greater than zero.
427	    ///
428	    /// [`Ink and Gas`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/concepts/gas-metering
429	    fn tx_ink_price(&self) -> u32;
430	
431	    /// Computes the units of gas per a specified amount of ink.
432	    fn ink_to_gas(&self, ink: u64) -> u64 {
433	        let price = self.tx_ink_price();
434	        if price == 0 {
435	            return 0;
436	        }
437	        ink / price as u64
438	    }
439	
440	    /// Computes the units of ink per a specified amount of gas.
441	    fn gas_to_ink(&self, gas: u64) -> u64 {
442	        gas.saturating_mul(self.tx_ink_price().into())
443	    }
444	}

446	/// Provides access to the ability to emit logs from a Stylus contract.
447	pub trait RawLogAccess {
448	    /// Emits an EVM log with the given number of topics and data, the first bytes of which should
449	    /// be the 32-byte-aligned topic data. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
450	    /// [`LOG0`], [`LOG1`], [`LOG2`], [`LOG3`], and [`LOG4`] opcodes based on the number of topics
451	    /// specified. Requesting more than `4` topics will induce a revert.
452	    ///
453	    /// [`LOG0`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a0
454	    /// [`LOG1`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a1
455	    /// [`LOG2`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a2
456	    /// [`LOG3`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a3
457	    /// [`LOG4`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a4
458	    fn emit_log(&self, input: &[u8], num_topics: usize);
459	    /// Emits a raw log from topics and data.
460	    fn raw_log(&self, topics: &[B256], data: &[u8]) -> Result<(), &'static str>;
461	}
462	
463	/// Provides access to the ability to emit typed logs from a Stylus contract.
464	pub trait LogAccess: RawLogAccess {
465	    /// Emits a typed alloy log.
466	    ///
467	    /// ```rust,ignore
468	    /// sol! {
469	    ///    event Transfer(
470	    ///        address indexed from,
471	    ///        address indexed to,
472	    ///        uint256 indexed token_id
473	    ///    );
474	    /// }
475	    ///
476	    /// self.vm().log(Transfer { from, to, token_id });
477	    /// ```
478	    fn log<T: SolEvent>(&self, event: T) {
479	        // According to the alloy docs, encode_topics_raw fails only if the array is too small
480	
481	        let mut topics = [WordToken::default(); 4];
482	        event.encode_topics_raw(&mut topics).unwrap();
483	
484	        let count = T::TopicList::COUNT;
485	        let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(32 * count);
486	        for topic in &topics[..count] {
487	            bytes.extend_from_slice(topic.as_slice());
488	        }
489	        event.encode_data_to(&mut bytes);
490	        self.emit_log(&bytes, count)
491	    }
492	}
493	
494	impl<T: RawLogAccess> LogAccess for T {}

[package]
name = "stylus-sdk"
keywords = ["arbitrum", "ethereum", "stylus", "alloy"]
description = "Rust smart contracts with Arbitrum Stylus"
readme = "../README.md"

authors.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
repository.workspace = true
version.workspace = true

[dependencies]
alloy-primitives.workspace = true
alloy-sol-types.workspace = true
cfg-if.workspace = true
clap.workspace = true
derivative.workspace = true
hex = { workspace = true, default-features = false, features = ["alloc"] }
keccak-const.workspace = true
keccak = ">=0.1.6, <0.2"

# local deps
mini-alloc = { workspace = true, optional = true }
stylus-proc.workspace = true
stylus-core.workspace = true
# Version floor: keeps alloy-primitives on a ruint patched for RUSTSEC-2025-0137.
ruint = { version = ">=1.17.1", default-features = false }
branches = { version = "0.4", default-features = false }
rclite = "0.4"

[target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")'.dependencies]

stylus-test = { workspace = true, optional = true }

[dev-dependencies]
paste.workspace = true
sha3.workspace = true
alloy-primitives = { workspace = true, default-features = false, features=["tiny-keccak"] }

[package.metadata.docs.rs]
features = ["default", "docs", "debug", "export-abi", "stylus-test"]

hostio = []

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stage only the code hunks or only the test hunks of one file.

usage: stage_hunks.py <file> code|tests
A hunk belongs to the tests when it starts at or after the first line of the
`#[cfg(test)]`-gated `mod tests` block of the new file.
"""
import re
import subprocess
import sys

path, mode = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
assert mode in ("code", "tests")

new_lines = open(path).read().split("\n")
# locate `mod tests {` and walk up over its attributes
idx = next(i for i, l in enumerate(new_lines) if re.match(r"^mod tests \{", l))
start = idx
while start > 0 and new_lines[start - 1].startswith("#["):
    start -= 1
tests_start = start + 1  # 1-based line number of the first attribute line

diff = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "diff", "-U0", "--", path], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
).stdout
parts = re.split(r"(?m)^(?=@@ )", diff)
header, hunks = parts[0], parts[1:]

selected = []
for h in hunks:
    m = re.match(r"@@ -(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@", h)
    old_start, old_cnt, new_start, new_cnt = m.groups()
    old_start = int(old_start)
    old_cnt = 1 if old_cnt is None else int(old_cnt)
    new_start = int(new_start)
    new_cnt = 1 if new_cnt is None else int(new_cnt)
    # for pure deletions the new_start points to the line before the change
    probe = new_start if new_cnt > 0 else new_start + 1
    is_test = probe >= tests_start
    if (mode == "tests") == is_test:
        selected.append((old_start, old_cnt, new_cnt, h))

# rebuild hunk headers with correct new-file offsets for the selected subset
out = [header]
delta = 0
for old_start, old_cnt, new_cnt, h in selected:
    body = h.split("\n", 1)[1]
    if old_cnt == 0:
        new_start = old_start + 1 + delta
    else:
        new_start = old_start + delta
    out.append(f"@@ -{old_start},{old_cnt} +{new_start},{new_cnt} @@\n{body}")
    delta += new_cnt - old_cnt
patch = "".join(out)
if not selected:
    print(f"{path}: no {mode} hunks")
    sys.exit(0)
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "apply", "--cached", "--unidiff-zero", "-"],
    input=patch, text=True, check=True,
)
print(f"{path}: staged {len(selected)} {mode} hunk(s) of {len(hunks)}")
EOF

7921d96 refactor(utils): add crate-level lints for the Stylus SDK 0.10 macros
The `#[storage]`/`#[public]` macros of SDK 0.10 check
`feature = "contract-client-gen"`, which this crate does not expose, so allow
`unexpected_cfgs` for the crate. With `export-abi` they also generate public,
undocumented ABI export items, so skip `missing_docs` for that feature only.

Restore the formatting of the usage example in the crate docs and make the
`test_utils` docs independent of the removed test framework.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

 contracts/src/test_utils.rs |  6 +++---
 2 files changed, 15 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)
...

index af55395..d25c40f 100644
--- a/contracts/src/lib.rs
+++ b/contracts/src/lib.rs
@@ -23,12 +23,16 @@ importing them:
 
 ```ignore

-use stylus_sdk::{alloy_primitives::{Address, U256}, prelude::*};
+use stylus_sdk::{
+    alloy_primitives::{Address, U256},
+    prelude::*,
+};
 
 #[entrypoint]
 #[storage]
 struct MyContract {
-    pub erc20: Erc20}
+    pub erc20: Erc20,
+}
 
 #[public]
 #[implements(IErc20<Error = erc20::Error>)]
@@ -82,8 +86,13 @@ impl IErc20 for MyContract {
     clippy::module_name_repetitions,
     clippy::used_underscore_items,
     clippy::unreadable_literal,
-    deprecated
+    deprecated,
+    // The Stylus SDK macros check for a `contract-client-gen` feature, which

+    unexpected_cfgs
 )]
+// The items that `#[public]` generates to export the ABI are undocumented.
+#![cfg_attr(feature = "export-abi", allow(missing_docs))]
 #![cfg_attr(not(any(test, feature = "export-abi")), no_std, no_main)]
 #![cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, feature(coverage_attribute))]

content.text:
The `utils` migration is finished on `agent/utils`. It has 14 commits on top of 7e36233, and the worktree is clean. A dry-run merge into `bench` is clean.

The whole crate still does not compile, with 83 lib errors in other agents' modules. `check` and `test --no-run` show no errors in my files. The `contract-client-gen` `unexpected_cfgs` warnings appear in my worktree until your root `check-cfg` change is committed.

I also rewrote my branch once (old tip 04dedd5) so your guidance sits in the right commits. Every commit ends with only the Haiku `Co-Authored-By` line.

**Verification:** to test my modules now, I built a scratch crate at `/tmp/bench/scratch/utils-iso2`. It symlinks my sources, uses your root manifest (alloy 1.6.0 plus the `check-cfg`), and compiles only `utils`. There, the crate gives:
- 170 of 170 lib tests pass.
- The `StorageSlot` doctest passes.
- Clippy is clean with `-D warnings -D clippy::all -D clippy::pedantic`, both with and without `--all-features`.
- `doc --all-features`, a wasm32 check and an `export-abi` check are clean.
- rustfmt nightly-2025-08-01 is clean.

Logs are `/tmp/bench/logs/utils-check.log` and `utils-test-norun.log`.

**Files changed:** all owned.
- `contracts/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/src/test_utils.rs` (docs only)
- `utils/{address,storage_slot,nonces,pausable,metadata}.rs`
- `utils/cryptography/{ecdsa,eip712}.rs`
- `utils/introspection/erc165.rs`
- `utils/precompiles/{mod,p256_verify}.rs`
- `utils/structs/{bitmap,checkpoints/mod,enumerable_set/{mod,element}}.rs`

`contracts/Cargo.toml` and `utils/math/*` needed no change.

**Commits** (oldest first, two per line):
- 931de20 crate docs + export-abi `missing_docs` | 3e29378 fmt metadata/element
- 134f11a address docs, `has_code` reuse | 2ceb2ac address tests
- 3c8198f storage_slot docs and doctest | 6ed7a1e storage_slot test
- b19d118 ecdsa/precompiles explicit host | bde2f33 ecdsa and p256 tests
- c518d69 IEip712 docs | 3c7cd59 eip712 test
- f9cc74d trait tags and docs | 85a8fea nonces and pausable tests
- 45b692a fmt struct modules | dd1df8e bitmap, checkpoint and set tests

**Signature changes:**
- `ecdsa::recover`: `context: impl StaticCallContext` becomes `&impl HostAccess<Host = VM>`, building `Call::new()` inside. The `pub(crate)` `p256_verify` changes the same way.
- `Precompiles` (trait and blanket impl): `TopLevelStorage` becomes `TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>`. Its method signatures are unchanged.
- Per api-map, already in core and reviewed:
  - `StorageSlot::get_slot` takes `context`.
  - `AddressUtils::function_delegate_call` and `verify_call_result_from_target` take `context`.
  - `AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr)` is `pub(crate)`.
  - `IEip712::chain_id` and `contract_address` are `&self` methods.
- Unchanged: `IErc165`, `INonces` and `IPausable` stay `#[public]`, `Pausable` and `Nonces` keep their method names, and there are no storage or ABI changes.
- I removed the test-only `TopLevelStorage` impls and `#[public]` wrappers.

**Test inventory** (`#[test]` attributes, before to after): address 0→7, ecdsa 3→7, eip712 2→2, math/alloy 6→6, nonces 4→4, pausable 9→9, p256_verify 3→3, storage_slot 1→1, bitmap 3→3, checkpoints 8→8, enumerable_set 15→15 (macro-expanded for 8 types).
- At runtime that is 159 (2 ignored) to 170 run, none ignored. Nothing was removed or merged.
- I added 7 `AddressUtils` tests, 4 `ecdsa::recover` tests, and log assertions in `pause_works` and `unpause_works`.
- The two ignored P256VERIFY tests now run. The valid-signature test mocks the precompile answer.
- The failed-verification vector has s > N/2, so it returns false before reaching the precompile and needs no mock.
- Every mock-using test registers a single mock right before its call, because of the shared return-data buffer.

**Guidance applied:**
- `#[allow(missing_docs)]` with a one-line reason on `IErc165`, `INonces` and `IPausable`.
- The `lib.rs` doc example names `erc20::Error` instead of `Self::Error`.
- The doc comment is back on `function_delegate_call`.
- I added no Cargo feature and no crate-level `unexpected_cfgs` allow, relying on your workspace `check-cfg`.

**Requests and notes:**
- `lib.rs` keeps `#![cfg_attr(feature = "export-abi", allow(missing_docs))]` for the undocumented items `#[public]` generates. CI's `--all-features` clippy needs it.
- Other owners should not glob-import `stylus_sdk::testing::*` next to `use super::*`. It re-exports `stylus_core::*`, including `Error`, which makes names ambiguous, so import `TestVM` explicitly.
- Unsure: I kept `TopLevelStorage` as a supertrait of `Precompiles`. It could be relaxed to `HostAccess` only.
